prompt.context: Your client is a large multi-national financial services company. A drop in financial activity as well as increasing regulation has caused its profitability to drop for 2 years in a row.
prompt.question: How would you recommend that the client reverse this trend?

clarifying_info.q: What type of financial institution is this?
clarifying_info.a: The company focuses mainly on asset servicing and asset management.

clarifying_info.q: Can you tell me more about the revenue side?
clarifying_info.a: The client believes it has already exhausted all possible avenues of revenue increase.

clarifying_info.q: Has the company tried reducing labor costs?
clarifying_info.a: The company recently laid off about 5% of its staff and has capped compensation; it does not believe it can reduce labor expense any further.

exhibits.title: Client Revenues and Expenses
exhibits.shows: A table comparing total revenue and total expenses for 2010 and 2011.

exhibits.title: Costs as a Percentage of Total Expenses (2011)
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing the client's cost breakdown by category to the industry average, expressed as a percentage of total expenses.

exhibits.title: IT Hardware Costs (2011)
exhibits.shows: A table listing per-unit costs for five hardware categories for the client vs. industry average, along with annual quantity purchased.

framework: Set up a profitability framework: Profit = Revenue - Costs (or P*Q - (FC + VC*Q))
Explore revenue: price, volume, mix across business lines
Explore costs: fixed vs. variable; break down by major cost category (labor, IT hardware/software, other)
Identify the largest cost gap vs. industry benchmark and size the opportunity
Develop actionable recommendations to close the gap

questions.prompt: After seeing Exhibit 1, how would you like to proceed — revenue or costs?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that revenue grew only marginally ($1,200M to $1,205M, +0.4%) while expenses rose from $890M to $910M (+2.2%), compressing profit from $310M to $295M. Given client has exhausted revenue levers, focus should shift to cost reduction. Candidate should ask to break down major cost categories.

math.answer: Profit declined by $15 MM over 2 years

questions.prompt: After seeing Exhibit 2, which cost category would you focus on and why? If client's IT costs were brought to industry average, what would the savings and profit impact be?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify IT Hardware and Software as the biggest relative gap: client is at 27% of expenses vs. industry average of 16% — an 11 percentage-point gap. Labor is the largest absolute category but has been addressed. Candidate should calculate potential IT savings and profit impact.

math.setup: Savings = (Client IT% - Industry IT%) x Total Expenses 2011 = (27% - 16%) x $910 MM; Profit impact = Savings / Current Profit
math.answer: Potential savings of ~$100.1 MM, representing a ~33.9% increase in profit

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, calculate the annual savings if the client renegotiates IT hardware contracts to industry average prices.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute (Client price - Industry avg price) x Annual quantity for each hardware category and sum them. Rounding is acceptable.

math.setup: For each category: Savings = (Client unit cost - Industry avg unit cost) x Annual quantity purchased
math.answer: Total annual savings of ~$4.33 MM from renegotiating IT hardware contracts to industry average prices

brainstorming.prompt: Why might the client's IT hardware and software costs be higher than competitors, and what can the client do to bring them down?

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Client is paying higher prices than competitors for the same hardware
Contracts were last renegotiated after 2005 merger and have not been updated since
Lack of competitive bidding has allowed vendor prices to drift above market

categories.name: Specifications
ideas: Client is buying higher-performance (more expensive) hardware than needed
Opportunity to reduce hardware specifications to match actual workload requirements

categories.name: Utilization / Volume
ideas: Client may be over-provisioning — e.g., issuing multiple computers per employee
Server utilization may be low; virtualisation or cloud migration could reduce unit needs
Software license counts may exceed active users

recommendation: Renegotiate IT hardware contracts to bring unit prices to industry average levels, yielding an estimated $4.3 MM in immediate annual savings
Investigate reducing hardware specifications where performance requirements do not justify premium pricing
Extend the contract renegotiation effort to other IT software and services contracts to capture the full ~$100 MM theoretical savings implied by closing the IT cost gap to industry average
risks: Renegotiation may take time and face vendor resistance, delaying savings realization
Reducing hardware specifications could impact employee productivity if done incorrectly
Regulatory requirements in financial services may constrain certain IT cost-reduction options
next_steps: Conduct a full IT contract audit to identify all contracts eligible for renegotiation
Benchmark hardware specifications against industry norms to identify downgrade opportunities
Explore server consolidation or cloud migration to reduce total unit purchases
Review other non-IT cost categories for similar benchmarking opportunities
